title: Streaming slot-merger scheduler for variable-length dialogs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: In mixed prompt/response length traffic (interactive chat + long-context prompts) our continuous batching scheduler creates many small partially-filled slots which increases KV cache fragmentation and raises GPU memory pressure. Symptoms observed: OOM spikes on p3d-like instances during midday traffic, elevated cold-hit fractions for KV entries, and 95th percentile tail token latencies slipping beyond 350 ms for throughput-sensitive customers.

Hypothesis: Introducing a streaming slot-merging pass that opportunistically coalesces compatible slots (same model version, compatible quantization, non-overlapping KV regions) at enqueue time will reduce the number of small slots, improve KV locality, and reduce per-GPU resident memory by lowering the number of duplicated KV slabs. This should reduce tail latencies and OOM incidents while keeping average latency stable.

Goals:
- Reduce KV fragmentation metric (kv_fragmented_slots_ratio) by >= 30% on mixed traffic.
- Reduce GPU memory headroom variance and peak usage by >= 10% on targeted instance types.
- Keep P50/P95 token latencies within current SLOs and reduce P99 regressions.

Design summary:
1) Slot-merger pass: a lightweight O(1) check at enqueue for candidate merging into an existing open slot on the same worker. Merge criteria include same model_id, identical quantization_profile_id, matching decode mode, and no overlapping live KV ranges (checked via compact interval Bloom). Preference for merging smaller tokens-in-flight into larger slots when sequence-length skew exceeds threshold.
2) Streaming coalescing window: micro-window of 4-6ms to allow last-microsecond coalescing across hot-shards without long queuing.
3) KV pool dedup: when slots are merged, we avoid duplicate KV slab allocation by linking to a shared KV reference with refcounting and deferred eviction stamps.
4) Memory-aware backpressure: if merged-slot memory would exceed per-GPU watermark, revert merge and mark slot for immediate dispatch (prevents headroom exhaustion).
5) Telemetry hooks: emit merged_slot_count, merge_fail_reasons (format: "watermark|incompatible-quant|kv-overlap|time-window"), and merged_kv_shared_bytes.

Experiment plan:
- Canary A: Internal synthetic mixed workload (40% short chat turns, 60% long prompts) on a 4-GPU cluster. Compare baseline vs slot-merger enabled. Run 24-hour stability test.
- Canary B: 5% production traffic on regional pool for 48 hours with traffic shadowing and safety kill-switch.
- Metrics: kv_fragmented_slots_ratio, merged_slot_ratio, merged_kv_shared_bytes, gpu_mem_peak_delta, tokens_per_second, p95_token_latency, p99_tail_events, OOM_count.

Implementation notes:
- Implementation in runtime/scheduler/streaming_merger.cc with a new lightweight in-memory bloom for KV interval checks (reference bloom_params in PR).
- New config flags: runtime.scheduler.enable_slot_merger (bool), runtime.scheduler.merge_window_ms (int), runtime.scheduler.merge_memory_headroom_pct (int).
- Backwards compatibility: default disabled; when enabled, feature-gate per-customer via routing policy.

Trade-offs & risks:
- Increased enqueue CPU overhead (target < 2% worker CPU). Mitigation: micro-benchmarked merger checks at ~150ns per enqueue in optimized build.
- Incorrect merge decisions could increase latency for some requests if merge delays dispatch. Mitigation: strict merge windows and memory watermark checks.
- Complexity for KV lifecycle: refcounting introduces potential leaks if not finalized on preemption. Added unit tests for finalizers and a TTL-based cleanup path.

Telemetry and alerting:
- New Grafana panel: "Slot Merger Health" showing merged_slot_ratio, merge_fail_reasons histogram, and merged_kv_shared_bytes over time.
- Alert: merge_fail_reasons:watermark rate > 5% sustained for 10m => rollback candidate.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature implementation + unit tests (this ticket).
2) Internal synthetic canary (Canary A) and perf regression run.
3) Small production canary (Canary B) with 5% traffic and automatic rollback on alert.
4) Gradual ramp to 50% over 72h if metrics stable.
5) Full enablement for customers with mixed-length traffic; add per-customer opt-in in console.

Acceptance criteria:
- Synthetic canary shows >= 25% reduction in kv_fragmented_slots_ratio and <= 5% CPU overhead.
- Production 5% canary shows no increase in p99 token latency and OOM_count==0 over 48h.
- All e2e tests and scheduler unit tests pass in CI.
